data.exact_reserve_text: An unfavorable run-off deviation (prior accident years' deterioration) of $121m for Syndicate 2003 was experienced during the year driven from various lines of business. The most significant contributors towards the adverse experience were London Wholesale Property ($58m), Energy ($32m) and US Workers' Compensation ($18m) accounts due to unfavorable claims experience.

named_events.event_name: Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria; Mexico earthquake; California Wildfires
named_events.loss_description: Collectively, these represented gross losses to the Syndicate of $1,015m. The Syndicate benefited significantly from external catastrophe reinsurance protection, as well as a whole-account stop loss (WASL) agreement. Net of all reinsurance and related reinstatement premiums, the total losses on these events was $290m.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2017 gross claims outstanding were $4,143.479m. During 2017 the Syndicate recorded an adverse prioryear runoff deviation of $121.0m (approximately 2.92% of opening gross reserves), driven primarily by adverse development in London Wholesale Property ($58m), Energy ($32m) and US Workers' Compensation ($18m). This movement represents a net strengthening of reserves for prior accident years.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development amount ($121m) is taken from the "Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding" narrative (explicitly stated). The balance sheet claims outstanding and movement figures are presented in $000s in the report and have been converted to millions. The $121m is presented as an aggregate gross prioryear deterioration in the narrative; the report does not provide a separate gross tabular 'prior year movement' number by accident year. A gross claims development triangle is present and was used to cross-check, but the narrative note is used as primary for prior year movement.
